In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MWC 297 seems to be a very young B1.5 star surrounded by a flat disk, still in the process of accretion and a wind, which is probably the first sign of the formation of a bipolar jet.
the disk and the wind are both present in the system.
MWC 297 appears as a classical T Tauri star with a disk, but with a strong stellar wind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disk is flat and optically thick, the wind is optically thin but optically thick in the polar direction, and the disk is not accreting at the moment.
the stellar wind is not confined to the equatorial plane, but extends to higher latitudes.
the AMBER instrument is a great tool for studying stellar winds and disks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wind appears to be much more extended and more massive than the disk, and that it dominates the line emission.
the disk and wind are not independent structures but rather that the wind is an extension of the disk.
the stellar wind is not a spherical outflow but is strongly affected by the presence of the disk.
